answer: Like a meadow where every new seedling must prove it can grow, an agent economy can require each agent to lock a meaningful stake in a time-locked vault before it may transact. The stake is released only after sustained honest work, and a crystal-clear public record ties each agent's history to its deposit. An attacker spawning thousands of fake agents must fund a vault for every one, so the cost of a Sybil swarm scales linearly while honest agents pay once, making forgery far more expensive than the fraud it could earn.
